groups.title: Cloze Test - Printing Press
groups.passage: The printing press, invented by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440, (A) the way information was shared. Before this (B) device, books were copied by hand, a process that was slow and expensive. Gutenberg's movable type (C) printers to produce books quickly and in large numbers. This (D) led to a dramatic fall in the cost of books. As a result, literacy (E) across Europe, and new ideas spread more (F) than ever before.

groups.title: Reading Comprehension - Developing Nations Energy
groups.passage:
Developing nations face a dual challenge: expanding access to electricity while limiting carbon emissions. For decades, fossil fuels dominated their energy mix, but the falling cost of solar and wind technology has begun to change this picture dramatically.

Solar power, in particular, has emerged as a game-changer. In many rural regions where extending the traditional grid is prohibitively expensive, small solar installations now bring light to homes that had never before been connected. These decentralised systems are often cheaper and quicker to deploy than large power plants.

Yet the transition is far from (I). Financing remains a major obstacle, as upfront costs deter households and small businesses. Governments in poorer countries frequently lack the capital to subsidise clean energy on the scale required, and international funding, though growing, is still inadequate.

Policy also plays a crucial role. Nations that have offered stable incentives and clear regulations have attracted far more investment than those with unpredictable rules. Political will, therefore, can be as important as technology in determining the pace of adoption.

Despite these hurdles, the momentum appears unstoppable. As prices continue to decline and awareness of climate risks grows, renewable energy is likely to become the default choice rather than a costly alternative for the developing world.

groups.title: Stacked Boxes Puzzle
groups.puzzleText:
Nine boxes J, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, R are stacked one above another.
- Only two boxes are below box J.
- Box P is immediately below box J.
- Box M is at the bottom.
- Box L is immediately above box J, and box O is immediately above box L.
- Box K is immediately below box N.
- Box R is at the top and box Q is immediately below box R.
- Three boxes are between box L and box Q.

groups.title: Month-Activity Puzzle
groups.puzzleText:
Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, G do seven different activities in seven months — January, March, April, June, August, October, December (in calendar order).
- Two people are scheduled between C and D.
- A goes in the month immediately after C.
- F goes in the month immediately before D.
- E goes in the last month.
- One person is scheduled between G and E.
- B goes in the month immediately before E.
- The person going in January likes Reading; A likes Painting; F likes Trekking; D likes Singing; G likes Cooking; the person in the last month likes Writing; B likes Dancing.

groups.title: Two-Row Seating
groups.puzzleText: Seven people sit in each of two rows. Row 1 (A, B, C, D, E, F, G) faces north; Row 2 (P, Q, R, S, T, U, W) faces south, and members of the two rows face each other position-for-position (position 1 of Row 1 faces position 1 of Row 2, and so on). Row 1 (positions 1→7, left to right): B, E, A, G, C, F, D. Row 2 (positions 1→7, left to right): T, P, W, S, R, Q, U. Facing pairs: B–T, E–P, A–W, G–S, C–R, F–Q, D–U.

groups.title: Age / Year Arrangement
groups.puzzleText:
Seven people P, Q, R, S, T, U, V were born in different years: 1960, 1968, 1972, 1980, 1985, 1990, 1998. (Older = born earlier.)
- R is the eldest.
- Only two people are elder to P.
- U is elder to P.
- One person was born between P and S.
- Q is elder to T but younger than S.
- V is elder to S.
- T is the youngest.

groups.title: Circular Table - City Puzzle
groups.puzzleText: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, G sit around a circular table facing the centre, each from a different city. Seated clockwise: A, C, E, B, G, D, F. Cities: A–Delhi, C–Pune, E–Kolkata, B–Mumbai, G–Jaipur, D–Chennai, F–Surat. (For a person facing the centre, left = clockwise, right = anticlockwise.)
